_source: ColdFusion Short, watched in the built-in browser 2026-11-18: frames at 0/0.5/1/2/3/5 s then every 3-4 s to the end, word timings from YouTube's transcript panel (about 190 words a minute). Our own descriptions. 89K views. Mostly a third party's own phone clip, re-posted with the channel's narration before it.

hook.firstFrame: plain black frame; a white news-headline card fades in at 1 s
hook.firstLine: AI that can copy any sound lets scammers claim others' songs.

shots.picture: a white news-headline card fades in near the top on black
the same headline card, lower on the black frame, still; voice only
a musician's own selfie clip in a forest playing a banjo; a white title box over her chest; word captions below
shots.onScreenText: title box: AI took her music, then blocked her

shots.picture: cross-fade into a second clip of the musician indoors
the musician's close-up selfie telling her story, captions word by word with one green or yellow word

lines.gist: AI voice copying lets fraudsters pass off others' songs as theirs
here is one case where the artist was powerless; tell me your view
a folk singer's songs were copied by AI, then her originals got claimed
in her words: a firm uploaded AI copies trained on her videos
the distributor then claimed her own videos, so her income stopped
she earns nothing from playing her own family's folk songs

ending.cta: asks viewers what they think (said at 12 s)

whyItWorks: A victim telling it in her own words carries the emotion; the channel only frames it.
The absurd turn (the copier claims the original) is the payoff.
Weak opening: 16 s of a still headline on black before any real picture.
